author: Akosa Samuel Onyejekwe (independent)
rule: Targets are stated here and are not loosened after a result is seen. docs/provenance.md gives the dated first record of each.

calibration.selection_rule: candidates in order of size: none, sensitive only, all. A larger set of fitted constants replaces the next smaller one only if its left-out cost is lower, averaged over the folds, by more than one standard error of the fold-by-fold differences
calibration.selection_rule_note: written on 2026-10-07 before the recalibration that follows the change of the pitch-rate source and of the static drag split; the earlier rule kept the candidate with the lowest total left-out cost, with no allowance for its scatter over folds. The first cross-validation had been seen when this rule was written

held_out_validation.group: held-out NACA 0012 loops inside the static Mach range whose peak incidence is inside the static lift range

origin.rule: each limit is the stricter of an absolute limit and 75 % of the baseline, the value the earlier form of the model had scored on the same held-out group when the targets were first recorded (2026-10-06 10:46 +03:00)
origin.note: copied on 2026-10-07 from the first recorded targets file, which the public file had reduced to the limits alone; the absolute limits and the damping-sign limit of 0.80 are the author's working limits for a model to be useful for section loads, not taken from a standard

code_quality.lint_rule_set: ruff rules F, E7, E9, B, C901, PLR0912, PLR0915

numerical.note: largest change in any normalised loop error of any calibration loop between the default resolution (dsmodel.march_resolution) and the finest march; this group was added on 2026-10-07, after the first record. From 2026-10-07 the step study is judged more strictly, against the Richardson-extrapolated value at zero step (results/convergence_extrapolated.csv); the limit itself is unchanged
numerical.state_space_note: largest difference in any normalised loop error of any calibration loop between the state-space form and the indicial march; added 2026-10-07 before the check was run on the calibration loops

equivalence_of_separation_laws.note: margin for calling the tabulated and the fitted separation law equivalent in the loads they predict with identical constants; written here before the direct load differences were computed, and after the differences between mean loop errors (at most 0.0021) had been seen
equivalence_of_separation_laws.quantity: RMS over the cycle of the difference between the two predicted coefficients, divided by the measured range of that coefficient over the loop; mean over the primary held-out loops
equivalence_of_separation_laws.test: upper end of the 95 % bootstrap interval of that mean below the margin, for each of the three sets of constants; and the 95 % interval of the paired difference in loop error inside plus or minus the margin
